### Course Descriptions

#### (0408704) Research Methodology in Islamic Sciences (3 hours)
This course aims to introduce, generally, the methodologies which Muslim scholars have applied in their research and books. It helps students understand the well-established methodology of research in Islamic sciences. The course highlights the rules of research, in addition to the mutable and changeable standards of research in this field of study. Furthermore, it aims to lead the student to a comparative study between this methodology and its encounter in the Western world. Moreover, this course assesses the methodology of research in contemporary legal, Fiqh, issues.

---

#### (0408705) Islam and Contemporary Issues (3 hours)
This course provides an in-depth study of contemporary issues involving Islamic religion, especially controversial subjects affecting Muslim peoples everywhere. Issues discussed may include but are not limited to the following: Islam and women; Islam and human rights; Islam and democracy; Jihad in Islam, including militant and theological interpretations of Jihad; as well as Western misconceptions about Jihad, the main obstacles to interfaith dialogues; Islam and minorities, in relation to both Abrahamic and non-Abrahamic religions.

---

#### (0408706) Islamic Sciences (3 hours)
This course examines the Quranic sciences, hermeneutics, and exegesis, muhkams and mutashabih. The usual al-Fiqh. Course concerns also include Muslims' strategies for reading the Quran; comparative analysis of Sunni and Shi’ite approaches to the Quran and Hadith; as well as discussion and analysis of the ethical implications of Islamic sciences.

---

#### (0408707) Islam and Interfaith Dialogue (3 hours)
The aim of this course is to clarify the true image of Islam, its spirit, its openness, and its universal dimension. It shows also the importance of reason and reasonable thinking and the significance of dialogue in the Quran and the Prophetic Tradition. It will have a more detailed and deep analysis of the concept of dialogue and its etiquettes from the Quranic perspective.

---

#### (0408708) Islamic Systems (3 hours)
The aim of this course is to shed light on the importance of Islamic systems, their main principles, characteristics, goals, the obstacles they faced, and their implementations throughout Islamic history. It will include some thorough analysis for economic, educational, political, and social Islamic systems.

---
